text_blocks.snippet: Synovial fluid monocytes are immune cells found in the fluid that lubricates joints. They play a role in both the body's defense and in the development of inflammatory joint conditions. In healthy joints, they contribute to maintaining tissue homeostasis, but in conditions like rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and osteoarthritis (OA), they can become activated and contribute to inflammation and joint damage.

text_blocks.snippet: Key aspects of synovial fluid monocytes:

list.title: Normal Function:
list.snippet: In healthy joints, synovial monocytes help to clear cellular debris (efferocytosis) and maintain tissue balance.

list.title: Activation in Disease:
list.snippet: In inflammatory arthritis, synovial monocytes can become activated, displaying markers of increased inflammation and contributing to the disease process.
